content.text:
The CLI tests are not broadly broken. The E2E workflow is red because three real-agent integrations failed for three external/harness reasons.

- [Claude Code job](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/33158583101/job/98807462174): 48/56 passed. The five failing scenarios all stopped at Claude’s workspace trust dialog. The harness only selects “yes” for the older `"Yes, I accept"` dialog. The new dialog says `"Yes, I trust this folder"`, so the harness presses Enter on the default `"No, exit"` choice and kills Claude. See [claude.go](/Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/cli-2/e2e/agents/claude.go:173).

- [Copilot job](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/33158583101/job/98807462229): 48/56 passed. Copilot v1.0.81 changed its interactive prompt, but the harness still waits for `❯`. Parallel Copilot tests also share `HOME`; its restore screen combines their sessions and reports `"Session ... is already in use"`. See [copilot-cli.go](/Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/cli-2/e2e/agents/copilot-cli.go:296).

- [Cursor job](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/33158583101/job/98807462240): only 6/56 passed because Cursor explicitly reports `"You're out of usage"`. This has been happening since at least Aug 25. It is an account quota problem, not an Entire regression.

The structural problem is that CI installs the latest Claude, Cursor, and Copilot releases on every run, with no version pins. See [e2e.yml](/Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/cli-2/.github/workflows/e2e.yml:90). There were no relevant harness changes between yesterday’s run where Claude and Copilot passed and this run. Their installed behavior changed underneath the repository.

That explains “all the time”: the last green main E2E run was [August 22](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/32583015061). Since then, Cursor quota and Gemini instability kept it red; after Gemini left the default matrix, Copilot v1.0.81 broke the prompt matcher, followed by Claude’s trust dialog.

Recommended fixes:

1. Restore Cursor quota or temporarily remove its job from required CI.
2. Update Claude’s startup handling to select `"Yes, I trust this folder"`.
3. Teach Copilot readiness detection about v1.0.81 and isolate its state per test. Running Copilot serially is a safe short-term workaround.
4. Pin tested agent versions, with a separate scheduled job for latest-version compatibility.
5. Keep deterministic E2E required, but treat live vendor-agent jobs as canaries unless the team wants vendor outages to block every merge.

I did not modify the repository or run paid E2E tests locally.
